plan: This is a second-price auction (I win and pay the second-highest bid if I have the highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With my value at $40, I should bid exactly $40.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. This mechanism makes truthful bidding a dominant strategy - bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid below my value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. My value is $13, so I should bid exactly $13.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value (negative profit). If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $17.
